new_statements.rule_in_words: Penultimate stress by default; if the penultimate nucleus is schwa, stress falls on the final syllable (prepenultimate nuclei are always schwa, so stress is confined to the last two syllables).
new_statements.exceptions: Schwa penults shift stress to the ultima. Note conflicting first-hand evidence for other Highland Kenyah varieties: Blust's 1971 Long Anap (Lepo' Sawa) notebook marks stress mostly final in citation forms; Blust 2013 sec. 4.1.3 areal remark (final stress in citation forms, penultimate in phrasal context) for coastal Sarawak and some interior languages.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement; snippet gives no information on citation vs phrasal context. CAVEAT: this is a SNIPPET-ONLY reading of a description of Lepu' Aga' (Lepo' Gah), a Baram-River (Sarawak) dialect of the same ISO language [xkl]/main1275 into which retired [knh] was folded; no statement of any kind was found for the Kayan-River (Apo Kayan: Lepo' Tau of Long Nawang, Lepo' Bem, Uma' Jalan, Bakung) varieties themselves.
new_statements.identity_note: kaya1334 'Kayan River Kenyah' [knh] is a Glottolog Bookkeeping languoid: ISO retired the code on 2008-01-14 (CR 2007-263) as a purely geographic label (Ethnologue 15: Apo Kayan highlands, Iwan River, Longbia; 'dialects' Lower Kayan Kenyah, Longbia, Kayaniyut, Long Nawan, Long Kelawit). Glottolog attributes any current use to Mainstream Kenyah [xkl] = main1275 'Usun Apau Kenyah'; the Apo Kayan / upper Kayan population speaks Lepo' Tau (Long Nawang), Lepo' Bem, Uma' Jalan, Uma' Tukung, Bakung, Lepo' Ma'ut etc., all main1275 (Bakung also = retired baku1265). It should not receive a catalog entry separate from main1275. The only stress statement quoted (Burkhardt 2006, snippet) describes Lepu' Aga' = Lepo' Gah of the Baram River, Sarawak (main1275, Glottolog dialect node lepo1241 area), not a Kayan-River variety; Blust's notebook evidence is for Long Anap (Lepo' Sawa, Baram); Blust 2017 fn. 11 is Western Lowland Kenyah (long1406); 'Kenyah (Blust 2007)' in handbooks is Oma Longh = Uma' Lung [ulu].
